articles.title: Micron-precision depth control in automated volumetric laser ablation with ultrashort laser pulses
articles.authors: Daniel Holder, Matthias Buser, Rudolf Weber, Volkher Onuseit, Thomas Graf
articles.summary: Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. …

articles.title: Low-frequency noise reduction in laser-induced graphene devices by noble metal nanoparticles decoration
articles.summary: We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sensors or contact paths in wearable electronics due to their elastic properties, and their inherent noise impacts their performance. The simple NPs modification of the LIG surface resulted in a noise-reduction effect, which increased in the following order: Pt<Ag<Au for the devices investigated here.​ Au-decorated LIG exhibited a 32-times reduction of normalized voltage noise. …

articles.title: Ion-Access Engineering for High-Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors
articles.authors: Wang J, Teuerle L, Chen L, Meier T, Sun T, Antrack T, Dong T, Zhang Z, Li P, Weissbach A, Solgi A, Kleemann H
institutions: Center of Smart Materials and Devices
articles.summary: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low-voltage operation and strong ionic-electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography-free ion-access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet-printed solid-state electrolytes. …
